triage.verifier_justification: I tried to refute this as mere generalization of a five-line pilot, and failed: the ch62 module claims chapter-wide scope (it keys every component off ch62_general_rate[hts_line]), yet its §122 exemption gate tested `entry_is_line_a or entry_is_line_b`, and `tools/b16_entry_flags.py` at the parent defines those flags as literal exemplar-line identity (`entry_is_line_a` = hts 7202111000, `entry_is_line_b` = 7601103000) while the same two flags simultaneously drive the China-301 list-1 and §232-aluminum slots — so the encoded population of "§122-exempt" was identical to "§301 list-1 member" and disjoint from the exception the rule's own proof atoms cite (the 9903.03.03 (aa)(ii) exclusion list and "articles of aluminum, of steel, or of copper or derivative aluminum or steel articles provided for in headings 9903.82.02 and 9903.82.04"). The Brazil and forced-labor gates show the same population error in the other direction: pre-fix they applied the duty to every entry of the listed origins except exemplar lines a/b, and the fix restricts them to `entry_is_brazil_301_listed` / `entry_is_forced_labor_301_listed`. This is a rule applied to the wrong set of tariff lines rather than an invented or ungrounded branch (the exception itself is sourced and survives the fix), so wrong_entity_or_scope fits better than untraceable_branch, and the PR's own "unlawfully suppressed" language plus its enumerated 18-cell witness-equivalence exception class rules out "enhancement only."

triage.verifier_notes: Caveats a reviewer should carry: (1) The correction is partial — post-fix ch62 still contains `entry_is_reciprocal_annex_excluded: formula: entry_is_line_a`, `entry_is_reciprocal_metals_excluded: formula: entry_is_line_b`, `+ (if origin_is_brazil and not entry_is_line_b: brazil_ieepa_additional_duty_rate else: 0)` (twice), and `+ (if entry_is_line_d and origin_is_china: list_1_additional_ad_valorem_rate else: 0)`, so the same exemplar-flag-as-membership-proxy defect survives in the IEEPA reciprocal and §338/beer surfaces. (2) Concretely for chapter 62 (apparel), the parent's entry_flags never set line_a..e true, so the observable pre-fix effect in this chapter was §301 always zero and §122 never suppressed; the "suppression on §301-member lines" is a property of the coupled encoding (one boolean serving both predicates) rather than of ch62 evaluation under the parent's flag generator — the scope defect holds either way, but do not restate the suppression as a ch62 evaluation result. (3) The fix trades over-application for documented under-application: `entry_is_brazil_301_listed`, `entry_is_forced_labor_301_listed`, `entry_is_china_301_2024_action`, `entry_is_china_301_solar` are hard-coded False in tools/b16_entry_flags.py pending membership tables. (4) The added `section_232_steel_component_rate` / `ch62_s232_steel_heading_rate` and their stack wiring are new coverage the module never claimed (PR: "a Section 232 steel component the witness never had") — not itself a defect correction — and land with a malformed nested `metadata: proof: proof: atoms:` that the PR issue comment says was repaired afterwards ("steel atoms unwrapped to canonical metadata.proof.atoms"). (5) Provision resolution through the pinned release (us-rulespec-2026-08-08-obbb-alien-snap, HTS 2026 Rev 3) does not reproduce the atoms' chapter-99 page-221/226/230 excerpts at those page paths, so the source check here rests on the module's own recorded excerpts, not on a re-resolved provision.
